paper.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

read_sources.note: Used for arXiv metadata, revision date, abstract, and ICML 2023 oral note.
Used to confirm ICML/PMLR publication metadata, pages, authors, and abstract.
Read for speculative execution framing, target/approximation models, distribution-preserving sampling, tasks, speedups, and limitations.

summary.one_sentence: Speculative decoding uses a faster draft model to propose several tokens, then verifies them with the slow target model in parallel so generation accelerates without changing the target distribution.
summary.thesis: The key observation is that autoregressive decoding is serial in target-model calls, but many next-token steps are easy enough for a cheaper approximation model to guess; the target model can verify a speculative prefix in one pass.
summary.why_it_matters: For agents, per-step latency compounds across tool loops, search, debate, retries, and self-consistency. Speculative decoding attacks the wall-clock cost of every generation without requiring a new target model.

prior_state: Generating K tokens from an autoregressive Transformer normally requires K serial target-model invocations.
Large target-model decode steps are slow and often limited by memory bandwidth or communication rather than raw arithmetic.
Adaptive computation methods can speed some cases but often require architecture changes, retraining, or accept changed output distributions.
Serving systems need latency improvements that work with existing off-the-shelf models.
problem.key_gap: The paper asks whether a small approximation model can propose tokens while a large target model verifies them in a way that preserves exact target-model sampling behavior.
assumptions: A faster approximation model is available and has enough agreement with the target model to be useful.
The target model can score multiple proposed tokens in parallel faster than running one serial decode step per token.
The sampling correction procedure is implemented exactly enough to preserve the target distribution.
Workloads benefit from lower serial target-model steps even if additional draft-model work is introduced.

concepts.name: Target model
concepts.definition: The large model whose output distribution the serving system must preserve.

concepts.name: Approximation model
concepts.definition: The smaller or cheaper draft model used to propose a speculative continuation.

concepts.name: Speculative prefix
concepts.definition: A sequence of candidate tokens produced by the approximation model before target-model verification.

concepts.name: Acceptance step
concepts.definition: The stochastic test that decides how many proposed tokens can be kept while preserving the target distribution.

concepts.name: Correction token
concepts.definition: A token sampled from an adjusted distribution when a proposed token is rejected.

concepts.name: Serial target runs
concepts.definition: The wall-clock critical path count of expensive target-model invocations.

method.core_idea: Generate a speculative token block with a cheap model, run the expensive target model once over that block to score all proposed positions, accept the longest prefix allowed by a distribution-preserving rule, and sample a corrected token when a draft token is rejected.
action_grammar: gamma: number of speculative tokens proposed per round.
draft token: token sampled from q.
target scores: p probabilities for the proposed positions computed in one target pass.
acceptance probability: min(1, p(token) / q(token)) for each proposed token under the algorithm.
residual distribution: adjusted target distribution used after rejection.
steps: Run the approximation model autoregressively for gamma draft tokens.
Run the target model once on the prompt plus speculative tokens to obtain target probabilities for all draft positions.
Walk through proposed tokens in order and accept each according to the speculative sampling rule.
If all proposed tokens are accepted, sample one additional token from the target model's next-token distribution.
If a proposed token is rejected, sample a correction from the residual distribution and stop the round.
Append accepted and corrected tokens to the output.
Choose approximation model and gamma to balance target-pass savings against rejected draft work.

claims.statement: Standard autoregressive decoding requires K serial target-model runs to generate K tokens.
caveats: Batching can improve throughput across requests, but not the serial dependency for one sequence's target-model steps.

claims.statement: Speculative decoding proposes several tokens with an efficient approximation model and verifies them using the target model in parallel.
caveats: Speedup depends on draft-model quality and target-model verification efficiency.

claims.statement: The algorithm preserves the target model's output distribution rather than merely approximating it.
caveats: This requires exact implementation of the speculative sampling/correction rule.

claims.statement: The method can accelerate off-the-shelf models without retraining or architecture changes.
caveats: It still requires access to a suitable smaller approximation model and integration with the serving engine.

claims.statement: On T5-XXL, the paper reports 2x-3x latency acceleration versus the standard T5X implementation with identical outputs.
caveats: The headline number is for the evaluated T5-XXL tasks and implementation.

claims.statement: The paper evaluates tasks/models including a 97M GPT-like model, 11B T5-XXL for translation and summarization, and a 137B LaMDA dialog model.
caveats: The paper's public wall-clock implementation comparison is emphasized for T5-XXL.

evidence.result: The paper states that decoding K tokens takes K serial runs of the large autoregressive target model.
The paper proposes sampling a speculative prefix from an efficient approximation model, then running the target model on those proposed tokens to verify them in parallel.

The authors state the speculative sampling method can generate several tokens concurrently without changing the target distribution, and Figure 1 illustrates fewer target runs with unchanged probability.
The abstract says the method accelerates existing off-the-shelf models without retraining or architecture changes.
The paper reports 2x-3x acceleration over the standard T5X implementation on T5-XXL with identical outputs.
The paper says it analyzes unconditional generation with a 97M GPT-like model, translation and summarization with 11B T5-XXL, and a dialog task with 137B LaMDA.

agent_infra_takeaways: Speculative decoding is a latency primitive for agent loops: every model call can return faster without changing the requested target distribution.
The draft model becomes serving infrastructure. It must be co-located, versioned, monitored, and chosen per target/workload.
Exactness matters for agent reliability. Speculative decoding's appeal is preserving outputs, not merely making a cheaper model answer first.
Speedup depends on acceptance rate. Hard reasoning, long-tail domains, or mismatched draft models can reduce gains.
Speculative decoding complements continuous batching and PagedAttention: one attacks serial depth, the others attack concurrency and memory.
For agent search, faster decoding lowers the cost of self-consistency, debate, reflection, and tree expansion.
caveats: The method needs a useful approximation model; a weak draft model can waste work.
The target distribution is preserved only if the sampling rule and probabilities are implemented exactly.
Speculative decoding reduces latency but does not reduce the semantic number of agent decisions.
Serving integration can be nontrivial because the draft and target models must share tokenization and efficient scheduling.
The method may interact with quantization, caching, batching, and structured decoding constraints in engine-specific ways.

related_work.title: Orca
related_work.note: Orca schedules token iterations across requests; speculative decoding reduces the number of target-model iterations on one request's critical path.

related_work.title: PagedAttention
related_work.note: PagedAttention makes large concurrent batches memory-efficient, while speculative decoding makes each sequence's serial target path shorter.

related_work.title: Self-Consistency
related_work.note: Speculative decoding can reduce the cost of sampling multiple reasoning traces from the same target model.
